title: 12  The Two Workflows
text:
12.2 Workflow 1: Model Creation

12.2.1 Theoretical Motivation
A naive approach to building a classifier would be to detect DMPs on all available samples, then evaluate the same classifier on held-out subsets. This conflates feature selection with performance estimation: the DMP panel was implicitly chosen to fit all samples, making any leave-out evaluation optimistic.
MethylValidation addresses this by repeating only the discovery portion of the pipeline on random train/validation splits. Each iteration rebuilds centroids and re-runs detection on the training cohort only. The resulting detector-side balanced accuracy summaries are used as internal estimates of discovery robustness and to filter stability runs when requested.
After many such iterations, a DMP that appears consistently in the discovery sets of most runs is more likely to reflect a true biological signal than one that appears in only a few. This motivates the stability analysis: the stable panel is a consensus over repeated random partitions of the data.
The production freeze then trains a final classifier on all available data restricted to the stable panel. Because the panel itself was selected using the full sample set (via the MC iterations), this is still an internal analysis; it is not a substitute for external validation on an independent cohort.


12.2.2 The Three Stages of Workflow 1
Workflow 1 is easiest to reason about as three explicit stages with different statistical roles.

12.2.2.1 Stage A — Stability (--stability)
Theoretical role. This stage estimates feature-selection stability rather than final predictive performance. Let \(\mathcal{D}_{\text{disc},r}\) be the discovery DMP set from split \(r\). A locus-level recurrence estimator
\[
\hat{f}(d) = \frac{1}{R^*} \sum_{r=1}^{R^*} \mathbf{1}[d \in \mathcal{D}_{\text{disc},r}]
\]
acts as a Monte Carlo approximation to selection probability under re-sampling. Thresholding with \(\hat{f}(d)\ge\tau\) (where \(\tau=\) stability_dmp_freq) enforces reproducibility pressure on the panel.
Practical role. This stage answers: “Which loci survive repeated train/validation perturbations?” In practice:

it runs only centroid -> detector per split (fast enough for many iterations),
it creates all_metrics.csv/metrics_summary.json for detector-side internal diagnostics,
it writes stability/stable_dmps_production.csv, which is the only accepted panel input for --freeze,
and it allows optional run-quality filtering via stability_min_balanced_accuracy before recurrence counting.

For most projects, this is the stage where panel size and robustness are tuned (n_iterations, train_fraction, stability_dmp_freq).


12.2.2.2 Stage B — Freeze/Analysis (--freeze)
Theoretical role. This stage converts the consensus panel into a deterministic production artifact. The key operation is a panel-constrained rerun on all samples: detector inference is no longer discovering a new panel; it is applying fixed loci and producing full downstream biological interpretation from a stable feature space.
Practical role. This stage answers: “Given a locked panel, what is the complete biological analysis on the full cohort?” In practice it:

injects fixed_dmp_panel into production/project.json,
rebuilds centroids on all data,
runs detector in fixed-panel mode,
runs mapper and enricher to produce gene/pathway outputs,
optionally runs progression synthesis for ordered disease-stage summaries.

The freeze artifacts (production/project.json, fixed-panel detection outputs, mapper/enricher summaries) become the canonical handoff package for model release and review.


12.2.2.3 Stage C — Modeling (--model)
Theoretical role. This stage fits the final prediction function conditioned on the frozen panel and frozen production project. It separates feature agreement (handled in Stage A/B) from final classifier parameter estimation (handled here).
Practical role. This stage answers: “What trained model artifacts should be deployed?” In practice it uses step_config.validation.model_backend:

ecdf (default): runs methyl-classifier then methyl-predictor,
tabular_sklearn: runs model bundle -> tabular training -> tabular predictor evaluation,
generative_hybrid: runs model bundle -> latent-density generative training -> generative predictor evaluation.

For all backends, the optional biological gate (require_biological_review_for_model) is enforced before model creation.
The resulting files under production/classifiers/ and production/predictors/ are the deployable model artifacts. Any rerun with changed panel or freeze inputs should be treated as a new model version.



12.2.3 Steps
Step 1: Prepare the project configuration
Ensure the project file has step_config.validation with at least train_fraction, n_iterations, seed, and run_stability: true:
"validation": {
  "train_fraction": 0.8,
  "n_iterations": 50,
  "seed": 42,
  "run_stability": true,
  "stability_dmp_freq": 0.7,
  "stability_min_balanced_accuracy": null,
  "abort_on_step_failure": false
}
Step 2: Run Monte Carlo with stability
source .venv/bin/activate
methyl-validation --project configs/project_Healthy_vs_PCa1-4-CG.json --stability
This runs n_iterations stratified train/validation splits. Per iteration:

methyl-centroid --group group1 and --group group2 build separate centroid H5 files for the training split.
methyl-detector --project detects DMPs between the training centroids.

After all iterations, stability analysis counts DMP recurrence across the discovery sets:
\[
\hat{f}(d) = \frac{1}{R^*} \sum_{r=1}^{R^*} \mathbf{1}[d \in \mathcal{D}_{\text{disc},r}]
\]
and writes monte_carlo_runs/stability/stable_dmps_production.csv.
Step 3: Run the production freeze
methyl-validation --project configs/project_Healthy_vs_PCa1-4-CG.json --freeze
This calls freeze_production_model() and then (optionally) progression synthesis which:

Merges stable DMP CSVs into monte_carlo_runs/production/stable_dmps_genomewide.csv.
Creates monte_carlo_runs/production/project.json with fixed_dmp_panel injected into step_config.detection.
Runs production freeze on all samples: centroid → detector(fixed panel) → mapper → enricher.
If step_config.progression.enabled=true, runs methyl-disease-progression to aggregate cross-stage mapper/enricher outputs.
Writes monte_carlo_runs/production/production_summary.json.

Step 4: Run final model build
methyl-validation --project configs/project_Healthy_vs_PCa1-4-CG.json --model
This runs run_pipeline_for_model():

methyl-classifier --project production/project.json
methyl-predictor --project production/project.json

If step_config.validation.require_biological_review_for_model=true, --model is blocked until biological_review_confirmed=true.

12.4 Diagnostic: DMP Coverage
Symptom. sample_dmp_coverage.dmps_used_fraction_median < 0.5 in validation_metrics.json. Values below 0.3 indicate severe degradation.
Cause. The centroid min_coverage (e.g. 4) and the detector min_sample_coverage (default 10) are mismatched. DMP positions that were detectable in training centroids at 4× coverage become invisible in test samples when the classifier requires 10× coverage.
Fix. In step_config.detection, add:
"min_sample_coverage": 4
This aligns the coverage requirement for classification with the centroid build threshold.
Verification. Re-run Workflow 2. dmps_used_fraction_median should rise to 0.6–0.9 for typical WGBS data.

title: 12  The Two Workflows
text:
12.5 Diagnostic: Class Imbalance
Symptom. The confusion matrix shows near-perfect recall for the majority class (e.g. healthy/control) and near-zero recall for minority classes (disease stages). Balanced accuracy is close to 1/K (random chance).
Cause. The training cohort has substantially more samples in one class. For example, 86 healthy vs 25–36 disease samples per stage (41% healthy in the example project). The multinomial logistic regression learned head defaults to the majority class when the histogram scores are ambiguous (which is common when DMP coverage is low).
Fix. In step_config.detection, add:
"multiclass_train_learned_head": true,
"multiclass_learned_class_weight": "balanced"
The balanced setting computes \(w_k = n_{\text{total}} / (K \cdot n_k)\), penalizing majority-class errors proportionally less than minority-class errors. See Section 5.9 for the full derivation.

title: 12  The Two Workflows
text:
12.6 Diagnostic: Sklearn Version Mismatch
Symptom. Warning messages during prediction: InconsistentVersionWarning: Trying to unpickle estimator LogisticRegression from version X.Y.Z when using version A.B.C.
Cause. The multiclass-classifier.pkl was serialized with a different version of scikit-learn than the one currently installed.
Diagnosis. Check the sklearn_version field in the model PKL metadata:
import pickle
with open("monte_carlo_runs/production/classifiers/multiclass-classifier.pkl", "rb") as f:
    model = pickle.load(f)
print(model["metadata"].get("sklearn_version"))  # version used at training time
Compare to the current installed version:
import sklearn; print(sklearn.__version__)
Fix. Re-run the --freeze step with the current sklearn version. The logistic regression head will be retrained and the new PKL will record the correct version. New model PKLs produced after the fix always record sklearn_version in their metadata.

title: 12  The Two Workflows
text:
12.7 Choosing Workflow Parameters

12.7.1 train_fraction
Higher values (0.8–0.9) leave less data for validation but produce more powerful centroids in training. For small cohorts (total \(n < 50\) per class), prefer 0.8. For large cohorts, 0.9 is reasonable.


12.7.2 n_iterations
More iterations reduce the variance of the empirical performance summaries. 20–50 iterations is typically sufficient to characterize the mean and standard deviation of balanced accuracy. 100+ iterations are useful for stable percentile estimates (e.g. p5, p95).


12.7.3 stability_dmp_freq
Higher values (0.8–1.0) produce smaller, more reproducible panels but may miss positions that are biologically informative but variable across splits. Lower values (0.5–0.7) retain more positions at the cost of including split-sensitive noise. A good starting point is 0.7.


12.7.4 stability_min_balanced_accuracy
Setting this parameter (e.g. to 0.6) excludes iterations with poor validation performance from the DMP frequency count. This can improve panel quality by excluding outlier runs where the centroid construction or detection failed to find informative DMPs. It also reduces the effective R* and thus increases the variance of \(\hat{f}(d)\). Use with caution for small n_iterations.

14.1.1 Software requirements

14.1.2 Environment setup
From the MethylPipeline repository root:

methyl-validation --help

cd /path/to/MethylPipeline

title: 14  User Guide
14  User Guide
text:
14.3 Workflow 1: Model Creation
Full theoretical background: Section 12.2.

14.3.1 Stage-oriented execution checklist
Workflow 1 should be run and reviewed in three explicit stages:

Stability (--stability): optimize panel robustness (n_iterations, train_fraction, stability_dmp_freq) and verify stable_dmps_production.csv is non-empty and biologically plausible.
Freeze/analysis (--freeze): lock the panel into production/project.json, then review production detector outputs together with mapper/enricher summaries.
Modeling (--model): train final classifier and predictor artifacts only after stability and biological review are complete.

Treat changes in any of these stage inputs as a model version change, not as a minor rerun.


14.3.2 Step 1: Run Monte Carlo with stability
source .venv/bin/activate
methyl-validation --project configs/my_project.json --stability
This runs n_iterations Monte Carlo discovery cycles (centroid → detector), then aggregates DMP recurrence frequencies.
Monitoring progress. Progress is shown via a Rich progress bar in interactive terminals. Iteration logs are written to monte_carlo_runs/run_000N/logs/.
Useful flags: - --iterations N — override n_iterations from config for a quick test run - --seed S — override the seed - --skip-enricher — skip enricher during --freeze (and progression, if enabled)


14.3.3 Step 2: Check stability results
After the loop completes, review the stability output:
cat monte_carlo_runs/stability/stability_summary.json
head monte_carlo_runs/stability/stable_dmps_production.csv
The summary reports: - n_runs_analyzed — number of qualifying runs - total_unique_dmps — total unique positions across all runs - stable_dmps_at_threshold — positions with frequency ≥ stability_dmp_freq
If stable_dmps_at_threshold is very low (< 1000), consider reducing stability_dmp_freq or increasing n_iterations.


14.3.4 Step 3: Run the production freeze
methyl-validation --project configs/my_project.json --freeze
This runs the production freeze pipeline on all samples using the stable DMP panel (centroid → detector(fixed panel) → mapper → enricher). Output is in monte_carlo_runs/production/.
If step_config.progression.enabled=true, freeze also runs methyl-disease-progression and writes production/progression/.


14.3.5 Step 4: Run the final model stage
methyl-validation --project configs/my_project.json --model
This runs classifier → predictor on the frozen production project.
If step_config.validation.require_biological_review_for_model=true, --model requires:
"biological_review_confirmed": true


14.3.6 Choosing the --model backend
By default, --model uses the ECDF backend (model_backend: "ecdf"). Advanced projects can choose a different backend in step_config.validation:

model_backend: "tabular_sklearn"
model_backend: "generative_hybrid"

CLI overrides are also available in methyl-validation for quick experiments (for example --model-backend generative_hybrid, --generative-latent-dim, --generative-density-type, --generative-calibrate).
Example:
"validation": {
  "model_backend": "generative_hybrid",
  "model_weight_column": "weight",
  "tabular_max_dmps": 5000,
  "generative_latent_dim": 16,
  "generative_density_type": "diag_gaussian",
  "generative_epochs": 50,
  "generative_batch_size": 64,
  "generative_seed": 13
}


14.3.7 Backend comparison (practical)









Backend
Best used when
Main strengths
Main risks / caveats




ecdf
You want continuity with historical MethylPipeline behavior and detector-classifier semantics
Native pipeline path, direct compatibility with existing classifier/predictor tooling, easiest interpretation relative to prior studies
Can underperform when class boundaries need stronger discriminative reshaping or additional covariates


tabular_sklearn
You want fast supervised baselines or covariate-aware tabular modeling from fixed DMP bundles
Simple deployment, mature sklearn ecosystem, often strong baseline performance with moderate tuning
Less directly tied to ECDF likelihood semantics; performance may depend strongly on feature cap (tabular_max_dmps) and model choice


generative_hybrid
You want likelihood-based latent modeling with posterior probabilities while preserving detector-driven weighting
Hybrid latent-density scoring, consistent DMP bundle contract, supports binary and multiclass posterior inference
More modeling complexity; requires careful reporting of latent/density settings and calibration choices for reproducibility



For manuscript methods sections, always report backend choice, key hyperparameters, and whether covariates were used.


14.3.8 Optional: Run progression synthesis as a standalone step
If your project has multiple ordered disease groups and you want a dedicated cross-stage summary after freeze, run:
methyl-disease-progression --project configs/my_project.json
Useful flags:

--ordered-comparison-labels pca_pca1,pca_pca2,pca_pca3,pca_pca4 to enforce explicit stage order
--strict-missing to fail when any stage input file is missing
--report-md to also emit a markdown summary report

Default output directory is production/progression/ when called from the freeze workflow, or <project_root>/progression for standalone runs.

14.7 Interpreting Results

14.7.1 all_metrics.csv
One row per successful iteration. Key columns:







Column
Description

Iteration index (1-based)


run_id
Directory name (e.g. run_0001)


accuracy
Overall accuracy


balanced_accuracy
Primary metric: mean per-class recall. More informative than accuracy for imbalanced datasets.


sensitivity
Recall for the positive class (binary mode)

Recall for the negative class (binary mode)

Macro-averaged F1 across all classes

Total validation samples

Number of classes





14.7.2 metrics_summary.json
For each metric in all_metrics.csv, reports:
{
  "balanced_accuracy": {
    "mean": 0.75,
    "std": 0.05,
    "min": 0.62,
    "max": 0.84,
    "count": 20,
    "p5": 0.65,
    "p25": 0.72,
    "p50": 0.76,
    "p75": 0.79,
    "p95": 0.82
  }
}
Interpreting balanced accuracy. For \(K\) classes, random chance gives \(1/K\) (0.2 for 5 classes). A production model with mean BA 0.75 and std 0.05 is substantially above chance. Publication claims should report mean ± std and the 95th percentile interval.


14.7.3 validation_metrics.json (per run)
Located at run_000N/predictors/validation_metrics.json. Contains:

accuracy, balanced_accuracy, confusion_matrix, per_class metrics
sample_dmp_coverage.dmps_used_fraction_median — critical diagnostic field (see below)
n_samples, n_classes, class_names



14.7.4 Confusion matrix interpretation
The confusion matrix is indexed [true_class][predicted_class]. A model biased toward the majority class (e.g. healthy) shows high recall for class 0 (all) and near-zero recall for all other classes. This is the primary symptom of class imbalance (Section 12.5).

title: 14  User Guide
text:
14.8 Three Key Diagnostics

14.8.1 Diagnostic 1: Low DMP Coverage
Symptom: sample_dmp_coverage.dmps_used_fraction_median < 0.5 in validation_metrics.json. All cancer classes predicted as healthy.
Root cause: min_sample_coverage in step_config.detection is higher than the centroid min_coverage in step_config.centroid.base_config.
Fix: Align both thresholds:
"centroid": { "base_config": { "min_coverage": 4 } },
"detection": { "min_coverage": 4, "min_sample_coverage": 4 }
Verification: After re-running, check dmps_used_fraction_median in the new run’s validation_metrics.json. Expected range: 0.6–0.95.
See Section 4.10 for theoretical background.



14.8.2 Diagnostic 2: Class Imbalance
Symptom: Confusion matrix shows recall ≈ 1.0 for the majority class (e.g. healthy/control) and recall ≈ 0 for all disease classes. Balanced accuracy close to 1/K.
Root cause: The training cohort has substantially more samples in one class. The multinomial logistic head defaults to the majority class when histogram scores are ambiguous.
Fix:
"detection": {
  "multiclass_train_learned_head": true,
  "multiclass_learned_class_weight": "balanced"
}
This sets \(w_k = n_{\text{total}} / (K n_k)\) in the logistic regression. Note that multiclass_train_learned_head: true is required for multiclass_learned_class_weight to take effect.
Verification: Re-run. The confusion matrix diagonal should become more balanced. Per-class recall should be non-zero for all classes.
See Section 5.9 for theoretical background.



14.8.3 Diagnostic 3: Sklearn Version Mismatch
Symptom: InconsistentVersionWarning during prediction. The model was trained with sklearn X.Y.Z but is being run with A.B.C.
Check:
import pickle, sklearn
with open("monte_carlo_runs/production/classifiers/multiclass-classifier.pkl", "rb") as f:
    model = pickle.load(f)
print("Trained with sklearn:", model["metadata"].get("sklearn_version"))
print("Current sklearn:     ", sklearn.__version__)
Fix: Re-run --freeze with the current sklearn version. The new PKL will be trained with the current version and record it in metadata.
Long-term: Pin scikit-learn to a specific version in your environment to avoid future mismatches.
